dedupe_keys.name: transport for london cyber attack august september 2024

description: This case covers the intrusion into the network of Transport for London (TfL) between 31 August and 3 September 2024, as set out in the National Crime Agency (NCA) news release on the sentencing of two members of the online criminal collective known as Scattered Spider, identified by the NCA and the City of London Police and prosecuted under section 3ZA of the Computer Misuse Act. Coverage: swift action by TfL limited the impact, but 148 systems became inoperable, including critical ones that needed significant manual workarounds; all 27,000 employees had to attend an office for a password reset; the Dial-a-Ride booking service for vulnerable Londoners, concessionary travel cards, the digital payments channel, Oyster refunds and photocard applications were disrupted, and the extension of contactless ticketing was delayed. TfL reported GBP 29 million in loss and recovery costs; the NCA says that shutting the network could have cost the UK economy up to GBP 56 billion. Format and access: a web news release. Licence and cost: free to read. Caveats: a law enforcement account, not a technical incident report. The affected systems and workarounds can define cyber-to-service dependencies in transit resilience and cascading failure models. It relates to the TfL Unified API and the Colonial Pipeline ransomware response in the catalogue.
